summary: Created an 8-phase implementation plan operationalizing the research report's cleanup sequence for the Logos/ProtonMail-Bridge maildir duplication and mbsync reconcile failures. The plan addresses two independent root causes: (1) removing Channel logos-labels from Group logos in ~/.dotfiles/modules/home/email/mbsync.nix (config fix, cross-repo, following the existing gmail-trash/gmail-spam exclusion precedent) to stop mirroring additive Bridge labels as local Maildir++ folders (.Labels.Important alone = 86% of the 43,660-file tree), and (2) Message-ID-based (NOT checksum-based) dedup of the separate, older duplicate-U=NNN corruption in .Trash/.Archive plus a narrow per-folder .mbsyncstate/.uidvalidity reset. Phases are sequenced conservatively for a partially-destructive cross-repo task: Phase 1 freeze+backup (email-freeze, mbsyncstate snapshot, per-folder tarballs, baseline counts) -> Phase 2 config fix + home-manager rebuild + ~/.dotfiles commit -> Phase 3 read-only redundancy-verification GATE (confirm no message exists only under a label, using filesystem enumeration not notmuch) -> Phase 4 remove orphaned .Labels.* mirror files (preserving any label-only messages) -> Phase 5 Message-ID-based Trash/Archive UID dedup + narrow state reset -> Phase 6 remove the headerless test message from .Sent (1771019138.#1M...hamsa,U=12:2,S) -> Phase 7 scoped `mbsync logos` reconcile (NEVER -a, NEVER /email --logos --sync before verified) to push the 161 staged Trash deletes -> Phase 8 notmuch reindex + consistency check + lift freeze. The dotted-folder crash on .Labels.benbrastmckie@gmail.com resolves as a side effect of Phase 2. Every destructive phase is gated behind verification and backed by Phase 1 snapshots; if Labels redundancy cannot be confirmed, Phase 4 leaves files inert rather than risk data loss.
decisions_made: Sized the plan as 8 phases (each ~0.5-1.5h, one agent run) with a 6-wave dependency map: freeze/backup (1) -> config fix (2) -> parallel-capable verification/dedup/test-message-removal on disjoint folder territory (3,5,6) -> Labels deletion (4, gated on verification 3) -> scoped reconcile (7, gated on all mutations 4/5/6) -> reindex (8).
Placed the config fix (Phase 2) BEFORE any maildir surgery so no further label-mirror bloat accumulates during cleanup, per the research report's explicit ordering.

Inserted a dedicated read-only redundancy-verification GATE (Phase 3) before the destructive Labels deletion (Phase 4), so bulk deletion only proceeds after confirming no message exists exclusively under a label; if verification is inconclusive, Phase 4 leaves the files inert (no data-loss risk).

Encoded the report's checksum caveat as a hard constraint: Trash/Archive dedup (Phase 5) keys on Message-Id and flags, never md5/fdupes, because Bridge injects copy-specific artifacts making logically-identical messages byte-distinct.
Scoped the mbsync state reset (Phase 5) to ONLY .Trash/.Archive, never the whole logos account, and required a snapshot-first backup in Phase 1.

Made Phase 7 reconcile explicitly scoped `mbsync logos` (never -a, never /email --logos --sync before verification) with a dry-run/verbose capture and a stop-on-failure resume policy rather than force-pushing.
dead_ends: Do not run /email --logos --sync at any point before Phase 7's clean reconcile is verified (explicit task prohibition).
Do not use content checksums (md5/fdupes) to dedup the .Trash/.Archive duplicate-UID pairs -- zero byte-identical duplicates exist across the tree; dedup MUST be Message-ID-based.
Do not reset the whole logos account's .mbsyncstate -- scope the reset narrowly to .Trash/.Archive only.

Do not trust notmuch path:/folder: counts as ground truth during verification -- use direct filesystem enumeration (find/ls/grep); the notmuch index-staleness issue is out of scope (tasks 823/824/827).
Do not re-add logos-labels to Group logos; keep the channel definition for optional manual inspection only.
Do not touch logos-folders (Proton Folders are exclusive, 0 files) or protonmail.nix.
